slides.headline: A family dinner. Look under the table.
Florence
slides.text: A dinner in Renaissance Florence. Isabella's rich brothers sit at the table with Lorenzo, a young man who works for them.

slides.headline: The lovers
slides.text: Lorenzo offers Isabella half of an orange on a plate. They are secretly in love, and think no one has noticed.

slides.headline: The kick
slides.text: But in the front, one brother stretches out his leg and kicks Isabella's dog under the table. His anger is building.

slides.headline: The nut
slides.text: He cracks a nut in his fist, staring at Lorenzo. The other brothers have seen everything too. Jealousy spreads.

slides.headline: The dog
slides.text: The little greyhound lays its head gently on Isabella's knee, the only one at this table truly on her side.

slides.headline: The story
slides.text: The story comes from Boccaccio and a poem by John Keats. Millais was only twenty when he painted it.

slides.headline: The friends
slides.text: Millais used his friends as models. The painter Dante Gabriel Rossetti is the man drinking from a tall glass.

slides.headline: Her choice
slides.text: Her brothers want her to marry for money. Would you choose the poor young man you love, against your whole family?
